question: After I export objects in Veeam Data Cloud, how do I get hold of the exported files, what format are they in, and is there a time limit on downloading them?
gold_facts: At the end of the export wizard you can enter a Reason for Export, which is saved to the session history.
Veeam Data Cloud creates a download link once the files are exported.
The exported files are JSON, compressed into a ZIP for download.
Download them from Activity > Restore Sessions > session details (See details here) > Download.
The download link is valid for 7 days; after it expires a new export session must be started.

A.text: After the export session completes, download the files by selecting Activity, then the Restore Sessions tab, clicking "See details here" in the Details column of the object export session, and clicking Download in the Session Details window [1][2]. The exported files are JSON files compressed in ZIP format [1][2]. The download link is valid for 7 days; when it expires, you must start a new export session [1][2].

documents.title: Step 4. Download Exported Files
documents.text:
Step 4. Download Exported Files
Step 4\. Download Exported Files

After Veeam Data Cloud completes the export session, download the exported JSON files. For download, the files are compressed in the ZIP format.

To download the exported files, do the following:

1. Select Activity.
2. Select the Restore Sessions tab.
3. In the list of sessions, click See details here in the Details column of the object export session.
4. In the Session Details window, click Download.

The download link is valid for 7 days. When the link expires, start a new export session.

B.text:
After exporting objects in Veeam Data Cloud, you can get the exported files in several ways depending on what you exported:

**How to get the files:**
- Veeam Data Cloud creates a download link after exporting files through the Export Users wizard [4], and provides a download link (SAS link) valid for 7 days [3]. Microsoft Azure Storage Explorer can be used to download exported log files using a shared access signature (SAS) link [6].
- For Salesforce records, the Export to CSV tool allows immediate download for up to 10,000 records; for 10,001 or more records, you receive an email with a download link valid for 18 hours [5].
- OneDrive folders and documents can be downloaded to a computer as a.ZIP file [8] [9].
- Mapping rules can be exported to a CSV file for download to the local machine [10], and the list of mapped fields can be exported as a CSV file to the default download folder on the local machine [15].
- Restore sessions activity information of the past 90 days can be exported as a CSV file download [14].

**Formats:**
- Exported files are compressed in ZIP format for download [2].
- Object export exports entire Entra ID objects to files in JSON format [7], and backed-up Microsoft Entra ID objects (such as users, groups, roles and so on) are exported to JSON files for further import or restore into Microsoft Entra ID or compatible systems [11].
- CSV export is available for Salesforce records [5], mapping rules [10], mapped fields [15], and restore session activity [14].

**Time limits:**
- The SAS download link is valid for 7 days [3].
- The email download link for large Salesforce exports (10,001+ records) is valid for 18 hours [5].
- Exported Sign-in Log files are available for download for 2 hours; when the time expires, a new restore session must be started [12]. The same 2-hour limit applies to exported Audit Log files [13].

documents.title: Entra ID Restore
documents.text:
[Entra ID Restore › Entra ID Restore]
Entra ID Restore
================

Veeam Data Cloud offers the following types of data restore:


* [User restore](entra_id_user_restore.html) — to restore entire users or their properties.
* [Group restore](entra_id_group_restore.html) — to restore entire groups or their properties.

* [Administrative units restore](entra_id_units_restore.html) — to restore entire administrative units or their properties.

* [Role restore](entra_id_role_restore.html) — to restore entire roles or their properties.

* [Application restore](entra_id_app_restore.html) — to restore entire applications, service principals or their properties.

* [Conditional Access policies restore](entra_id_cap_restore.html) — to restore entire Conditional Access policies or their properties.
* [Microsoft Intune policies restore](entra_id_intune_restore.html) — to restore entire Microsoft Intune policies or their properties.

* [Log export](entra_id_log_restore.html) — to export audit and sign\-in logs.
* [Object export](entra_id_object_export.html) — to export entire Entra ID objects to files in JSON format.


With Veeam Data Cloud, you can also compare properties of the following objects:

* [Microsoft Entra ID organization contacts](entra_id_contacts_compare.html)
* [Entra ID devices](entra_id_devices_compare.html)


Veeam Data Cloud allows you to view and copy BitLocker recovery keys. For details, see [Viewing BitLocker Recovery Keys](entra_id_devices_view_bitlocker.html).

documents.title: Configuring Restore Mapping Settings
documents.text:
[Configuring Restore Mapping Settings › Configuring Restore Mapping Settings]
Object IDs Mapping

When restoring a record that was deleted from Salesforce, Veeam Data Cloud creates a new record in Salesforce, assigns a new ID to this record and populates its fields with the values of the record from the backup. To associate the newly created record with the backed\-up record, Veeam Data Cloud creates a default rule that maps the ID of the backed\-up record with the ID of the record created in Salesforce. 

You can delete a mapping rule if you no longer need it. When a mapping rule is deleted, Veeam Data Cloud will create a new record version. It is recommended that you delete mapping rules in a sandbox environment only.

To delete a mapping rule, do the following:

1. On the Salesforce page, click the name of the tenant you want to manage.
2. To view all restore jobs created for the tenant, select Restore on the left.
3. Select the necessary job.
4. Select Settings \> Object IDs Mapping.
5. In the Restore Setting: Object IDs Mapping window, do the following:


1. Specify the ID of the record saved in the backup, the ID of the existing Salesforce record or both, and click Find Existing Mapping.
2. Click Remove.
3. Click Save to confirm that you want to remove the mapping rule.


| Tip |
| --- |
| To export the list that contains all mapping rules created for the restored records, click Export to CSV. Veeam Data Cloud will export all the mapping rules to a CSV file and download it to your local machine. |

documents.title: Entra ID Object Export
documents.text:
[Entra ID Object Export › Entra ID Object Export]
Entra ID Object Export
======================

You can export backed\-up Microsoft Entra ID objects (such as users, groups, roles and so on) to JSON files for further import or restore into Microsoft Entra ID or compatible systems.
 The exported data includes all object properties, relationships and a relevant schema. Veeam Data Cloud also exports sensitive data if it was backed up.


You can export only one object type at a time. If you want to export more object types, run a separate export session for each object type.

To export objects, do the following:


1. [Launch the Export Objects wizard](entra_id_object_export_launch.html).
2. [Select the restore points](entra_id_object_export_point.html).
3. [Finish working with the wizard](entra_id_object_export_summary.html).
4. [Download the exported files](entra_id_object_export_download.html).

documents.title: Viewing Restore Sessions
documents.text:
[Viewing Restore Sessions › Viewing Restore Sessions]
Viewing Restore Sessions
========================

You can view all Flex and Express restore sessions and their details in the Activity page.

Only users with the OrganizationAdmin or M365:Administrator roles or a custom role with the View Activity Logs and View Restore Activity permissions can view the Restore Sessions tab in the Activity page of their tenant. For more information about roles, see [Roles](users_roles.html).  

To view the list of restore sessions, do the following:

1. On the Microsoft 365 page, click the name of the tenant you want to manage.
2. Select Activity.
3. Go to the Restore Sessions tab.

In the Restore Sessions tab, in the restore sessions list, Veeam Data Cloud displays the following information for each restore session:

**Viewing Restore Sessions**

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Activity Type | Veeam Data Cloud displays the type of the restore activity and the restored object type in the Restore Type (object type) format. The available restore types are: Restore, Copy, Download, Export. The available object types are: Exchange, OneDriveBusiness, SharePoint, Teams. For example, for a restore session of a SharePoint site, Veeam Data Cloud will display the following activity type: Restore (SharePoint). |
| Status | The status of the restore session. |
| Start | The date and time the restore session was started. |
| Finish | The date and time the restore session was completed. |
| Actor | The email address of the user that triggered the restore session. |

[

![Viewing Restore Sessions](/media/ef1dcf3b-bf8b-49dc-bc99-d856cd12f6a7/1503b23b85ba.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Activity page in Microsoft 365 Org, showing the 'Restore Sessions' tab with a list of recent restore, copy, and export activities. Each entry includes activity type, status (Started, Success, Warning), start and finish times, and the actor's email address.

](images/m365_activity_restore.png "Viewing Restore Sessions")


| tip |
| --- |
| You can click Export to download a .CSV file with the restore sessions activity information of the past 90 days. Select the date range of activity you want to export and click Submit. The file is downloaded to your Downloads folder. |

documents.title: Step 6. Configure Additional Restore Settings
documents.text:
[Step 6. Configure Additional Restore Settings › Step 6. Configure Additional Restore Settings]

Field Mapping Settings

In the Field values section, you can choose whether you want Veeam Data Cloud to populate fields of a restored record with values of a specific backed\-up record. To do that, click the link in the Map old fields to new fields field, choose an object whose field values you want to overwrite, and map the necessary backed\-up record fields to fields in the target Salesforce tenant. For an object or a field to be displayed in the list of available items, it must have a backup.

To export the list that contains all mapped fields as a CSV file, click Export to CSV. Veeam Data Cloud will save the file with the exported data to the default download folder on the local machine.


| Important |
| --- |
| * For security reasons, mapping of encrypted fields is not supported. * Overriding and mapping fields of the Text (Encrypted) type is not supported. |


Blocking Automation Settings

Business logic and automated rules configured in Salesforce can block Veeam Data Cloud restore operations or trigger undesirable side processes. You can choose either to manually deactivate Flows, Validation Rules, Workflow Rules, Lookup Filters, Process Builders and Apex Triggers in Salesforce or to instruct the product to bypass all blocking automation while performing a restore operation. To do that, select one of the options in the Turn off automation section:


* Select the I will manually turn off all blocking automation option, if you are a Salesforce Administrator and want to deactivate Flows, Validation Rules, Workflow Rules, Lookup Filters, Process Builders and Apex Triggers in Salesforce manually.

question: As a service provider on Veeam Data Cloud for Azure, I've just added a customer's Azure tenant and want to protect their Azure SQL databases. When can I start working in that tenant, and what network gotchas will hit the first SQL backup policy runs?
gold_facts: A newly added Azure tenant appears on the Azure Management page with Provisioning status.
The tenant's management dashboard is accessible only after Veeam provisions backup infrastructure to the tenant.

If public access is disabled on the SQL Server, the first policy run tries to create a private endpoint connection and fails; the connection request must be approved in the Azure portal or the policy keeps failing.
If public access is enabled on an Azure SQL Managed Instance, the policy uses the public endpoint, requiring inbound port 3342 open, even if a private endpoint is also configured.

A.text:
Based on the available sources, I can address the network gotchas, but not the tenant onboarding timing.

**Network gotchas for first SQL backup policy runs:**

- If public access is disabled on the customer's SQL Server, the backup policy will attempt to create a private endpoint connection during the first run, which will initially fail. You must approve this connection request in the Azure portal for future policy runs to succeed; otherwise, the policy will continue to fail [1][3].
- If public access is enabled on an Azure SQL Managed Instance, the backup policy will use the public endpoint, which requires port 3342 to be open for inbound connections, regardless of whether a private endpoint is also configured [1][3].

**On when you can start working in the tenant:** The sources do not describe any onboarding delay or waiting period after adding a customer's Azure tenant, so I don't have enough information to answer that part from the available sources.

documents.title: Considerations and Limitations
documents.text:
Considerations and Limitations

| Important |
| --- |
| Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support Microsoft Azure features that are currently in the preview state. For more information, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/project/navigation/preview-features?view=azure-devops). |

Before you start using Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure, review the following limitations and considerations for protecting VMs, Azure SQL Servers and Azure Files.

General

Consider the following about backup and restore of Azure resources:

* To store backups, Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure automatically creates a repository in every Azure region whose resources are protected by the backup policy.
* Due to Microsoft Azure limitations, Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support retention of locked snapshots. This means that Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure will not be able to remove an outdated snapshot during a retention session if the snapshot is protected from deletions and modifications using the lock feature. For more information on the lock feature, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources?tabs=json).
* Backup is not supported for Microsoft organizations in US Government GCC High regions.

Azure VMs

Consider the following about backup and restore of Azure VMs, VM disks and files:

* Consider the following about backup of Azure VMs deployed in virtual networks with restricted (private) access:

* If VM disks have restricted network access, Veeam Data Cloud will temporarily modify the networking configuration to allow public SAS link access during the backup, which will enable the creation of snapshots with preserved network settings. Once the backup transfer is complete, the network settings are reverted to their original state.
* If network access is completely denied, Veeam Data Cloud will not be able to modify this setting, which will result in backup failure.

* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support backup of Azure VMs whose source disks have the data access authentication mode enabled. For more information on the data access authentication mode, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/download-vhd?tabs=azure-portal#enable-data-access-authentication-mode).
* Due to Microsoft Azure limitations, Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support backup of [Ephemeral OS disks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/ephemeral-os-disks#unsupported-features).

* When performing restore operations, Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure assigns Azure tags to the processed resources. If you have any Azure policies that do not allow tag assignment, the restore operations will fail. To learn more about Azure policies, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview).

* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support restore of Azure confidential VMs. For more information on Azure confidential VMs, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/confidential-vm-overview).
* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure does not support restore of locked Azure VMs and Azure virtual disks. For more information on the lock feature, see [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources?tabs=json).

Azure SQL Databases

Consider the following about backup and restore of Azure SQL databases:

* You can create SQL backup policies to protect only Azure SQL databases running on SQL Servers and databases located on SQL Managed Instances. If you want to protect a database hosted by a SQL Server on Azure VM, create an [Azure VM backup policy](azure_backup_create_vm.html). Note that in this case, you will not be able to restore a single database without restoring the entire VM.
* Consider the following about backup of Azure resources deployed in virtual networks with restricted (private) access:

* If public access is disabled on the SQL Server, the backup policy will attempt to create a private endpoint connection during the first run, which will initially fail. You must approve this connection request in the Azure portal for future policy runs to succeed; otherwise, the policy will continue to fail.
* If public access is enabled on an Azure SQL Managed Instance, the backup policy will use the public endpoint, which requires port 3342 to be open for inbound connections, regardless of whether a private endpoint is also configured.

documents.text:
Creating SQL Backup Policies

Use the New Azure SQL Policy wizard to create a backup policy to protect SQL databases.

| Important |
| --- |
| Consider the following:* If public access is disabled on the SQL Server, the backup policy will attempt to create a private endpoint connection during the first run, which will initially fail. You must approve this connection request in the Azure portal for future policy runs to succeed; otherwise, the policy will continue to fail. * If public access is enabled on an Azure SQL Managed Instance, the backup policy will use the public endpoint, which requires port 3342 to be open for inbound connections, regardless of whether a private endpoint is also configured. |

1. [Launch the New Azure SQL Policy wizard](azure_backup_create_sql_launch.html).
2. [Specify the policy details](azure_backup_create_sql_name.html).
3. [Specify the policy source](azure_backup_create_sql_source.html).
4. [Specify the policy protection settings](azure_backup_create_sql_sla.html).
5. [Specify the database processing settings](azure_backup_create_sql_process.html).
6. [Review the default policy settings](azure_backup_create_sql_review.html).
7. [Specify the notification settings](azure_backup_create_sql_notifications.html).
8. [Complete the backup policy configuration](azure_backup_create_sql_complete.html).

B.text:
**Veeam Data Cloud:** To start protecting Microsoft Azure resources, you must add the customer's Microsoft Azure tenant to Veeam Data Cloud [8]. Once added, the tenant appears on the Azure Management page in the list of workload tenants with a Provisioning status [7], and Veeam Data Cloud creates an Azure application that acts as a service principal in the Azure tenant [6]. As a customer of a Veeam Cloud & Service Provider partner, you can choose whether to allow the partner to manage Veeam Data Cloud users, work with backup policies and restores, and configure tenant settings in the organization [5]; Veeam Data Cloud also offers provider-managed onboarding for these tasks [3].

**Network gotchas on first SQL policy runs:** If public access is disabled on the SQL Server, the backup policy will attempt to create a private endpoint connection during the first run, which will initially fail [1][2]; the connection request must be approved in the Azure portal for future policy runs to succeed [1][2]. The Azure SQL Policy wizard makes this same private endpoint connection attempt on the first run, which will initially fail [4].

**Microsoft:** Azure Backup requires network connectivity on the VM that hosts the SQL Server instance [13][11]. For SQL Server databases on Azure VM, it requires connectivity to the Azure Backup service, Azure Storage, and Microsoft Entra ID, achievable via private endpoints or by allowing access to required public IP addresses or FQDNs [14]. It also requires an inbound NSG rule allowing the service tags azurebackup, azurecloud, and storage [15], and routing backup extension traffic through an HTTP proxy server when backing up a SQL Server database on an Azure VM [16]. For service providers, Azure Backup supports Azure Lighthouse for managing delegated customer subscriptions [10], and CSP partners working on behalf of a tenant must specify the customer's tenant ID or primary domain name in Connect-AzAccount [9].

documents.title: Onboarding Customers
documents.text:
[Onboarding Customers › Onboarding Customers]
Onboarding Customers
====================

After you create a customer and assign a subscription in VCSP Pulse, you can onboard the subscribed customer and add their tenants to Veeam Data Cloud. Alternatively, you can invite your customers to add their tenants to Veeam Data Cloud and complete the onboarding process themselves. Veeam Data Cloud allows you to add multiple tenants to a workload using a single customer subscription.


Veeam Data Cloud will configure your access to the Veeam Data Cloud organization of the customer depending on the onboarding method you choose for the first tenant in the customer organization.


* If you choose provider\-managed onboarding, Veeam Data Cloud allows you to manage Veeam Data Cloud users, work with backup policies and restores and configure tenant settings in the Veeam Data Cloud organization of your customer.
* If you choose customer\-managed onboarding, Veeam Data Cloud prevents you from managing the Veeam Data Cloud organization of your customer.


The customer can change this setting. For details, see the [Configuring Partner Access](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vdc/userguide/sp_partner_access.html) section of the Veeam Data Cloud User Guide.
 Regardless of this setting, you can always add tenants and invite customers to add tenants to their organizations.


In This Section

* [Provider\-Managed Onboarding](sp_customers_onboard_managed.html)
* [Customer\-Managed Onboarding](sp_customers_invite.html)

documents.title: Backup
documents.text:
[Backup › Backup]
Back up Azure Files using Azure PowerShell
==========================================

This article describes how to use Azure PowerShell to back up Azure Files through an [Azure Backup](backup-overview) Recovery Services vault. You can also back up Azure Files using [Azure portal](backup-azure-files), [CLI](backup-afs-cli), and [REST API](backup-azure-file-share-rest-api).

Prerequisites
-------------

Before you back up Azure Files, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:

* [Learn more](backup-azure-recovery-services-vault-overview) about Recovery Services vaults.
* Review the Az.RecoveryServices [cmdlet reference](/en-us/powershell/module/az.recoveryservices) reference in the Azure library.
* Review the following PowerShell object hierarchy for Recovery Services:

![Recovery Services object hierarchy](/media/79636006-2202-4f15-824b-4407b15d721b/4bc71bde9d8e.png)

> **Figure:** Diagram showing the object hierarchy for Recovery Services, with RecoveryServicesVault at the root. It branches into BackupProtectionPolicy (linked to BackupRetentionPolicy), BackupManagementServer, BackupContainer (linked to BackupItem, which links to BackupRecoveryPoint), and BackupJob (linked to BackupJobDetails).

Set up PowerShell
-----------------

Note

We recommend that you use the Azure Az PowerShell module to interact with Azure. To get started, see [Install Azure PowerShell](/en-us/powershell/azure/install-azure-powershell). To learn how to migrate to the Az PowerShell module, see [Migrate Azure PowerShell from AzureRM to Az](/en-us/powershell/azure/migrate-from-azurerm-to-az).

Note

Azure PowerShell currently doesn't support backup policies with hourly schedule. Use Azure portal to apply this feature. [Learn more](manage-afs-backup#create-a-new-policy)

Set up PowerShell as follows:

1. [Download the latest version of Azure PowerShell](/en-us/powershell/azure/install-azure-powershell).

Note

The minimum PowerShell version required for backup of Azure Files is Az.RecoveryServices 2\.6\.0\. The latest version, or at least the minimum version helps you avoid issues with existing scripts. Install the minimum version by using the following PowerShell command:

```
Install-module -Name Az.RecoveryServices -RequiredVersion 2.6.0

```
2. Find the PowerShell cmdlets for Azure Backup by using this command:

```
Get-Command *azrecoveryservices*

```
3. Review the aliases and cmdlets for Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery, and the Recovery Services vault. Here's an example of what you might see. It's not a complete list of cmdlets.

![List of Recovery Services cmdlets](/media/79636006-2202-4f15-824b-4407b15d721b/ed2b5a0ef1b7.png)

> **Figure:** A PowerShell console output showing a list of Azure Recovery Services cmdlets, including their command type, name, version, and source module, generated by the command `Get-Command *azrecoveryservices*`.
4. Sign in to your Azure account by using **Connect\-AzAccount**.
5. On the webpage that appears, you're prompted to enter your account credentials.

Alternatively, you can include your account credentials as a parameter in the **Connect\-AzAccount** cmdlet by using **\-Credential**.

If you're a Cloud Service Provider (CSP) partner working on behalf of a tenant, specify the customer as a tenant. Use their tenant ID or tenant primary domain name. An example is **Connect\-AzAccount \-Tenant "fabrikam.com"**.

[Back up SQL Server instance snapshot › Back up SQL Server instance snapshot]
Prerequisites
-------------

Before you back up a SQL Server instance snapshot, review the following prerequisites:

* Identify or [create a Recovery Services vault](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#create-a-recovery-services-vault) in the same region and subscription as the VM hosting the SQL Server instance.
* Verify that the VM has [network connectivity established](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#establish-network-connectivity).
* Ensure that the SQL Server databases follow the [database naming guidelines for Azure Backup](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#database-naming-guidelines-for-azure-backup).
* Ensure that .NET 4\.6\.2 version or higher is installed on the VM.
* Confirm that you don't have any other backup solutions enabled for the database. Disable all other SQL Server backups before you back up the database.

documents.title: Tutorial for SQL Server on Azure VM backup
documents.text:
[Tutorial for SQL Server on Azure VM backup › Tutorial for SQL Server on Azure VM backup]
Tutorial: Back up a SQL Server database on an Azure VM
======================================================

This tutorial describes how to back up a SQL Server database running on an Azure virtual machine (VM) to an Azure Backup Recovery Services vault.

In this tutorial, you use the Azure portal to:

* Create and configure a vault.
* Discover databases and set up backups.
* Set up auto\-protection for databases.
* Run an on\-demand backup.

Prerequisites
-------------

* Identify or [create](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#create-a-recovery-services-vault) a Recovery Services vault in the same region or locale as the VM that hosts the SQL Server instance.
* [Check the VM permissions](backup-azure-sql-database#set-vm-permissions) that you need for backing up the SQL Server database.
* Verify that the VM has [network connectivity](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#establish-network-connectivity).
* Check that your SQL Server databases are named in accordance with [naming guidelines](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#database-naming-guidelines-for-azure-backup) for Azure Backup.
* Verify that you don't have any other backup solutions enabled for the database. Disable all other SQL Server backups before you set up this scenario. You can enable Azure Backup for an Azure VM, along with Azure Backup for a SQL Server database running on the VM, without any conflict.

sources.paraphrase: Azure Backup requires connectivity to the Azure Backup service, Azure Storage, and Microsoft Entra ID for SQL Server databases on Azure VM, which can be achieved using private endpoints or by allowing access to required public IP addresses or FQDNs.

documents.title: Azure Backup guidance and best practices
documents.text:
[Azure Backup guidance and best practices › Azure Backup guidance and best practices]
### Internet connectivity

* **Azure VM backup**: All the required communication and data transfer between storage and Azure Backup service happens within the Azure network without needing to access your virtual network. So back up of Azure VMs placed inside secured networks don't require you to allow access to any IPs or FQDNs.
* **SAP HANA databases on Azure VM, SQL Server databases on Azure VM**: Requires connectivity to the Azure Backup service, Azure Storage, and Microsoft Entra ID. This can be achieved by using private endpoints or by allowing access to the required public IP addresses or FQDNs. Not allowing proper connectivity to the required Azure services might lead to failure in operations like database discovery, configuring backup, performing backups, and restoring data. For complete network guidance while using NSG tags, Azure firewall, and HTTP Proxy, refer to these [SQL](backup-sql-server-database-azure-vms#establish-network-connectivity) and [SAP HANA](backup-azure-sap-hana-database#establish-network-connectivity) articles.
* **Hybrid**: The MARS (Microsoft Azure Recovery Services) agent requires network access for all critical operations \- install, configure, backup, and restore. The MARS agent can connect to the Azure Backup service over [Azure ExpressRoute](install-mars-agent#azure-expressroute-support) by using Microsoft peering, using [private endpoints](install-mars-agent#private-endpoint-support) or via [proxy/firewall with appropriate access controls](install-mars-agent#verify-internet-access).

sources.paraphrase: Azure Backup requires an inbound NSG rule to allow service tags azurebackup, azurecloud, and storage on Azure Network Security Groups for network traffic between Azure resources.

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]

* If you are using [Azure policies in your AKS cluster](/en-us/azure/aks/policy-reference), ensure that the extension namespace *dataprotection\-microsoft* is excluded from these policies to allow backup and restore operations to run successfully.
* If you are using an Azure Network Security Group (NSG) to filter network traffic between Azure resources in a virtual network, configure an inbound NSG rule to allow the service tags *azurebackup*, *azurecloud*, and *storage*. Allowing these service tags enables the AKS cluster to communicate with Azure Backup services and the associated storage account required for backup operations. Allowing inbound TCP traffic on port 443 is sufficient for all three service tags.
* Ensure outbound connectivity from the AKS cluster to Azure Backup and Storage endpoints is not blocked.

Required roles and permissions
------------------------------

To perform AKS backup and restore operations as a user, you need to have specific roles on the AKS cluster, Backup vault, Storage account, and Snapshot resource group.

| Scope | Preferred role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AKS Cluster | Owner | Allows you to install Backup Extension, enable *Trusted Access* and grant permissions to Backup vault over the cluster. |
| Backup vault resource group | Backup Contributor | Allows you to create Backup vault in a resource group, create backup policy, configure backup, and restore and assign missing roles required for Backup operations. |
| Storage account | Owner | Allows you to perform read and write operations on the storage account and assign required roles to other Azure resources as a part of backup operations. |
| Snapshot resource group | Owner | Allows you to perform read and write operations on the Snapshot resource group and assign required roles to other Azure resources as part of backup operations. |

sources.paraphrase: Azure Backup requires routing backup extension traffic for Azure Backup, Azure Storage, and Microsoft Entra ID through an HTTP proxy server when backing up a SQL Server database on an Azure VM.

documents.title: Back up multiple SQL Server VMs from the vault
documents.text:
[Back up multiple SQL Server VMs from the vault › Back up multiple SQL Server VMs from the vault]

#### Use an HTTP proxy server to route traffic

When you back up a SQL Server database on an Azure VM, the backup extension on the VM uses the HTTPS APIs to send management commands to Azure Backup and data to Azure Storage. The backup extension also uses Microsoft Entra ID for authentication. Route the backup extension traffic for these three services through the HTTP proxy. Use the list of IPs and FQDNs mentioned above for allowing access to the required services. Authenticated proxy servers aren't supported.

Note

Disable proxy for localhost communications within the VM. Proxy will be honored for outbound communications from the SQL VM.

### Database naming guidelines for Azure Backup

* Avoid using the following elements in database names:

	+ Trailing and leading spaces
	+ Trailing exclamation marks (!)
	+ Closing square brackets (])
	+ Semicolon (;)
	+ Forward slash (/)
	+ Percentage (%)
* SQL Backup configuration doesn't support the single quotation in the database name and causes deployment failure. If there's any database with single quote, we recommend that you rename the database or take the native backup approach.
* Aliasing is available for unsupported characters, but we recommend avoiding them. For more information, see [Understanding the Table Service Data Model](/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/understanding-the-table-service-data-model).
* Multiple databases on the same SQL instance with casing difference aren't supported.
* Changing the casing of a SQL database isn't supported after configuring protection.

Note

The **Configure Protection** operation for databases with special characters, such as `{`, `'}`, `[`, `]`, `,`, `=`, `-`, `(`, `)`, `.`, `+`, `&`, `;`, `'`, or `/`, in their name isn't supported. You can change the database name or enable **Auto Protection**, which can successfully protect these databases.

Create a Recovery Services vault
--------------------------------

A Recovery Services vault is a management entity that stores recovery points that are created over time. It provides an interface to perform backup\-related operations. These operations include taking on\-demand backups, performing restores, and creating backup policies.

To create a Recovery Services vault:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/).
